assessments.reasoning: ISC’s HTTPS licensing page returned the scoped body SHA-256 04614458f85b33964830d3d4eeed3cb220c8aa00d2af86675abb3a5b3da5ac55. The reported digest for [14093,14992) matches the citation. Under “Text of the ISC License:” the publisher gives two notices, © 2004-2013 by Internet Systems Consortium, Inc. (“ISC”) and © 1995-2003 by Internet Software Consortium. The grant says “use, copy, modify, and/or distribute this software” and requires the copyright and permission notices in all copies. Both disclaimer clauses name ISC. The preceding permission concerns “this License text for any purpose with or without fee”. Its parenthetical “like SPDX: 0BSD” describes that separate permission. The page identifies the displayed reference, while the SPDX identifier and release attribution depend on the other sources.

The official spdx/license-list-data detail was retrieved at commit 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48. The reported digest for [2184,3318) matches the citation. The fields name “ISC License” and give licenseId “ISC”. The first seeAlso URL and order-0 crossRef URL are both https://www.isc.org/licenses/. Both ISC URLs have match “false” and the OSI URL has “N/A”. All three are recorded as valid and live at the recorded check time. The generated licenseText uses “and/or”, a generic “Copyright <year> <owner>” notice and “THE AUTHOR” in both disclaimer clauses. The template makes the title and “/or” optional, allows the copyright pattern .{0,5000}, and uses .+ for each author field. Its fixed grant retains the notice condition. Both comment fields date the change from “and” to “and/or” to July 2007. These fields document identification, links and permitted textual variation. Release attribution requires the tag.

GitHub’s HTTPS Git Tags API for the official spdx/license-list-data repository returned the full 700-byte annotated-tag record. The reported SHA-256 for [0,700) matches the citation. The tag object’s own Git ID is 76c9a79bb7d2bf851143b76b3935a4d7cbaa644b, its tag field is “v3.29.0”, and its message names version 3.29.0 of the SPDX License List. Its target has type “commit” and SHA 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48, exactly the commit in the raw ISC.json URL. Repository origin supports attribution of the record to the official upstream. GitHub reports verified=false, reason “unsigned”, and null signature, payload and verified_at. The tagger field names Steve Winslow, but the unsigned record supplies no cryptographic authentication of the tagger. The tag establishes the release-to-commit link only.

challenge.method: Compared the full annotated tag’s name, Git object ID, target type and target SHA with the repository and commit segment of the detail URL. Examined whether the detail alone contained release metadata. Compared the cited publisher block with the detail’s identifying fields, both source-link fields, generated text, template and wording-history comments. Tested whether the recorded match values or notice differences contradict the claimed relationship.
challenge.results: The annotation names the requested release and points directly to the detail URL’s commit. The detail alone leaves the release unproven. The publisher link is explicit even though SPDX records its match value as the string “false”. That value and the observed wording differences preclude treating the link as an affirmative exact-text match. They do not contradict the claim that this entry cites this named publisher display.

limitations: The crosswalk applies to the captured publisher display and the entry at the specified commit. The tag-object endpoint establishes the recorded annotation and target. A later change to the live tag ref or publisher page would require fresh evidence.

The publisher HTML and generated SPDX text differ in their notices and disclaimer wording. Neither the link nor the matching template establishes byte identity or legal equivalence, including the legal effect of the earlier “and” wording.
The publisher’s permission to reuse the license text has a different object from the displayed software grant. Applying a license to particular code requires evidence for that code and version.
reasoning: Under SCES-1.0 at ab26f278422772f2d9e5d4dd016407d14372a710, for the supplied bundle SHA-256 14da3f31f697ab828d4a4560f060dbe511861020db54bea7bc531e20ea0855ce, the three original sources support the descriptive crosswalk. SPDX’s annotated tag v3.29.0 identifies the exact commit used to retrieve ISC.json. At that commit, the entry names “ISC License”, gives the identifier “ISC”, and cites the same publisher URL where ISC labels and displays the “and/or distribute” text. The tag and detail share SPDX upstream lineage. The tag establishes release attribution, the detail establishes entry identity and the source link, and the publisher establishes what the linked page displays.
